elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in Section 1.4: "The Company may, upon written notice to HDI, permit its affiliates to exercise the Company's rights of access and use under this Section 1.4." Coverage is conditioned on notice, so it satisfies the affiliate concept at the fallback standard rather than an unconditional preferred grant.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 1.4 as rendered names only "the Company" and its "affiliates"; no contractor or agent language was added. To reach the preferred level the drafter would have to add "and contractors acting on the Company's behalf" to the inserted sentence.
Section 1.4 grants access and use rights for the hosting arrangement with no perpetuity language, and no perpetual-term wording was inserted.
No "irrevocable" qualifier appears in Section 1.4 or elsewhere in the rendered language; the absence of an express at-will revocation right is not the same as an affirmative irrevocability covenant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered redline leaves the termination architecture untouched (Section 4.1 ninety-day notice remains, per the rationale); no language limits termination of the access/use rights to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.3: the Agreement "shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns" — no Vendor-consent gate is imposed, so the grant runs to successors and assigns generally.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Company may, upon written notice to HDI, permit its affiliates to exercise the Company's rights of access and use under this Section 1.4." The trigger (written notice to HDI) is defined and unilateral — no HDI consent required.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 is retained and contains no anti-assignment prohibition; it expressly makes the Agreement enforceable by the parties' "successors and assigns", which covers an M&A successor. The "no other person" tail restricts third-party beneficiaries, not successors named in the same sentence.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice is created by the single inserted sentence in Section 1.4, and successor/assign transfer is already preserved by the retained Section 10.3, so the position is complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level remains incomplete on four elements — contractors acting on our behalf, perpetuity and irrevocability of a paid-up licence, and termination limited to uncured material breach. If the team wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the new Section 1.4 sentence, and add an express statement that the access and use rights are irrevocable and terminable only for uncured material breach that remains uncured after notice.

Minimality holds: one concise sentence added, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language, procedures or other extras, and no duplication — Section 1.4 previously ran to "the Company" alone, so there is no existing affiliate coverage being restated.

Intent is preserved: the new sentence is framed as the Company permitting affiliates to exercise the Company's own Section 1.4 rights, which avoids collision with the retained Section 10.3 sentence that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement". No undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradicted retained sentence results; the Section 4.1 notice mechanic and all commercial terms survive intact.

Drafting note (not a defect): "affiliates" is not a defined term in this Agreement, and the reviewing team may prefer to anchor it (e.g. entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with the Company) to remove any argument about scope at the notice stage.

Finding status "deviation" is correctly classified — before the redline the grant ran to "the Company" alone with no path to add affiliates, failing the fallback; it is not walk-away because HDI has no express at-will revocation right.
